task_instance: Diagnose a suspected deadlock / thread-starvation in a running JVM application by following the skill's Tier 1 workflow: identify the target JVM with jps, then capture a live thread dump with 'jcmd <pid> Thread.print' (which also reports deadlocks), and analyze the captured dump to name the symptom.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is symptom-first RUNTIME diagnostics of a live JVM using JDK command-line tools (jps, jcmd, jstack, jmap, jstat, JFR, async-profiler, NMT, etc.). Producing the deliverable requires two abilities this office-assistant runtime does not grant: (1) a running Java/JVM process to target, and (2) executing shell commands / running the JDK diagnostic binaries to attach to that process and capture data. The runtime can only read/write/edit text files and fetch web pages; it cannot run any code, scripts, or shell commands. Without command execution there is no way to invoke jcmd/jstack against a PID and no way to produce or capture any diagnostic artifact. Per the task's own definition, 'running any code or command, installing software, or producing binary files counts as missing.' I could only hand-write the commands as text, not run them or verify any real output, so the actual deliverable (captured, verified runtime diagnostic data and a data-backed diagnosis) cannot exist.
evidence: Read the skill at skills/r131/skills/java-diagnostics/SKILL.md. It is entirely about executing JDK diagnostic tools against a live JVM: the Decision table maps symptoms to concrete commands (e.g. 'jcmd <pid> Thread.print', 'jstat -gcutil', 'GC.class_histogram -all=true', JFR 'JFR.start', heap dumps via 'GC.heap_dump'); the Permission tiers section is framed around 'May run after stating the exact command' / 'before running'; the Workflow step 3 is 'Collect data to a dedicated directory'. The chosen minimal task (capture a thread dump of a running JVM with jcmd and analyze it for a deadlock) needs both a live JVM process and shell execution of the JDK tool. Neither is available: no process to target and no command-execution capability in this runtime. Writing the commands into a text file is not running them and yields no verifiable deliverable. No sample input file substitutes for this, because the deliverable is data captured from a live process, not analysis of user-supplied documents.
